newsitem.title: USA: GTE earnings rise 10 percent, stock jumps.
newsitem.headline: GTE earnings rise 10 percent, stock jumps.

text.p: GTE Corp. Wednesday said its earnings rose 9 percent in the third quarter, boosted by strong demand for new phone lines from people setting up businesses or hooking up computers at home.
The results were in line with expectations, but GTE's stock rose more than $2 as investors were encouraged by the report from the nation's largest local telephone company.

On Tuesday, GTE and other local phone companies won a key ruling when a federal appeals court suspended key parts of a federal rule mandating local phone competition. Analysts said the ruling not only could delay competition in local phone business, but also could postpone entry of the Baby Bells into long distance service.
In addition to strong line demand, GTE cited growth in its cellular and long-distance services.

The Stamford, Conn.-based company said net income rose to $756 million, or 78 cents a share, in the quarter ended Sept. 30, from $695 million, or 72 cents a share, in the 1995 period. Sales grew 7 percent to $5.34 billion from $5.0 billion.
The 1995 results included a gain of $11 million, or 1 cent a share, from the sale of secondary telephone properties.
The results matched analysts' forecasts of 78 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks estimates. But GTE jumped $2.375 to $41 at midday on the New York Stock Exchange.
"The continued pace of our revenue growth, driven by record line growth as well as strong demand for new and enhanced services, is particularly encouraging," Chairman Charles Lee said in a statement.
The number of domestic access lines grew 7 percent in the quarter, with more than half the growth in the residential side of the business from additional lines to the home, GTE said.
GTE said its number of cellular customers grew almost 5 percent in the quarter, while cellular revenue surged 15 percent.
It also said it doubled its number of long-distance customers to more than 500,000 from the end of the second quarter.
